papers.title: ANN-based Monte Carlo simulation framework for reliability assessment of steel structures
papers.abstract: Reliability assessment of steel structures in accordance with EN 1990 requires the evaluation of very low failure probabilities. Direct Monte Carlo estimation using high-quality nonlinear finite element (FE) models is often computationally prohibitive because of the large number of simulations required. This paper proposes and validates an artificial neural network (ANN)-based Monte Carlo framework, providing a step-by-step procedure for surrogate development, model selection, and statistical validation. ANNs replace repeated FE analyses within the Monte Carlo procedure, using stochastic inputs generated through Latin Hypercube Sampling. Two resistance problems with different input dimensionality and physical mechanisms are investigated, each with independent stochastic inputs and a single governing limit state: Column Web in Compression (CWC) and slender welded I-girders under pure compression. Validation uses FE benchmark datasets generated separately from, and not used in, ANN training, comprising 50000 CWC cases and 5000 cases for each of seven I-girder cross-sections. The selected CWC models closely reproduce the FE resistance predictions across the full benchmark, with differences below 1% in the investigated lower-tail resistance quantiles. For the I-girders, comparison with the FE-based reference assessment shows that the ANN framework reproduces the calculated partial factors with small differences and enables the investigation of substantially larger simulation samples. For the 50000-case CWC assessment, the ANN-based approach reduces the total computational effort from approximately six months of parallel FE simulation to at most five days, including FE training-data generation, ANN training, and subsequent stochastic evaluation. These findings demonstrate the practical benefit of the framework and provide a promising basis for its further development and benchmarking for structural reliability assessment.

papers.title: Spontaneous Intrasinus Bone Formation Associated With Substantial Dental Implant Protrusion: A 22-Year Follow-Up Case Report
papers.abstract: Bone formation within the maxillary sinus has been reported following intentional membrane elevation, with or without bone grafting. Proposed contributing factors include graft osteoconduction, blood clot organization, space maintenance, and local osteogenic activity. However, long-term radiographic evidence suggestive of spontaneous bone formation following unplanned protrusion of a substantial portion of a dental implant into the maxillary sinus remains limited. This case report describes a 65-year-old female patient who underwent placement of a 5-mm-diameter, 13-mm-long Brånemark System Mk IV TiUnite wide-platform implant (Nobel Biocare AB; Gothenburg, Sweden) in the maxillary left first molar region. During surgery, additional apical advancement was required to achieve clinically satisfactory primary stability, resulting in approximately 8 mm of implant protrusion beyond the native bony sinus floor, as estimated from postoperative periapical radiography. No intentional sinus floor elevation or bone grafting was performed, although inadvertent displacement of the Schneiderian membrane could not be excluded. Resonance frequency analysis (RFA), performed using the Osstell system (Osstell AB; Gothenburg, Sweden), demonstrated high implant stability during healing, with an implant stability quotient (ISQ) of 74 at approximately month 7, followed by values of 79 and 80 at approximately months 8.5 and 9, respectively. At month 18, periapical radiography revealed increased radiopacity adjacent to the implant apex, suggestive of possible intrasinus bone formation. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), performed incidentally for an unrelated implant treatment plan approximately 19.5 years after placement, demonstrated mineralized tissue surrounding the previously protruding implant apex, with features compatible with spontaneous bone formation. Clinical follow-up extended to approximately 22.6 years. These observations suggest that mineralized tissue may develop and remain radiographically detectable around an implant protruding substantially into the maxillary sinus without planned sinus augmentation or grafting. Potential mechanisms include blood clot organization, space maintenance, and osteogenic activity from adjacent native bone or membrane-associated tissues. However, the absence of histological confirmation and standardized serial three-dimensional imaging prevents definitive conclusions regarding the tissue's biological origin, formation mechanism, and continuous volumetric stability.

papers.abstract: This study applies surrogate-model-based and Bayesian optimization to aeroelastic tailoring of composite laminates, aiming to maximize the critical aeroelastic instability velocity. A solver-coupled workflow integrates MSC Nastran analysis with MATLAB optimization, enabling comparative benchmarks across unidirectional (UD) laminates and curvature-constrained tow-steered designs. For all optimized configurations, flutter remained the governing aeroelastic instability. The results show that both optimization strategies recovered essentially the same optimum for UD tailoring, demonstrating cross-method consistency. For the composite plate wing, the optimized UD configuration increased flutter velocity from 26.48 to 46.30 m/s, while tow steering provided only a 0.11% increase (46.30 to 46.35 m/s), indicating no meaningful additional flutter benefit. For the AGARD 445.6 wing, UD optimization increased flutter velocity from 305.38 m/s to 378.32 m/s, with tow steering increasing flutter velocity to 390.0 m/s (+3.09%). These findings indicate that the benefit of tow steering is geometry-dependent: negligible for the composite plate wing but modest for the swept AGARD wing. Surrogate-model-based optimization proved effective in low-dimensional UD problems, whereas Bayesian optimization reduced evaluation counts in higher-dimensional tow-steering cases by automatically identifying coefficient bounds. Overall, this study demonstrates that both optimization workflows recovered consistent aeroelastic tailoring solutions, with tow steering offering limited incremental benefit beyond optimized UD laminates.

papers.abstract: Early‐age concrete undergoes internal humidity evolution accompanied by shrinkage deformation, both of which are closely related to non‐uniform volume changes and cracking risk. The humidity diffusion equation, self‐desiccation effect, boundary/initial conditions, and dual‐Kelvin shrinkage formulation are embedded into the framework. A non‐dimensional governing system and neural tangent kernel‐based adaptive weighting strategy are introduced to balance partial differential equation (PDE) residuals, constraints, and data losses. The model is validated using experiments, finite element method, and conventional PINN predictions. AWPINN accurately captures humidity gradients and shrinkage evolution, achieving a predicted‐to‐measured internal relative humidity ratio of 0.98, with errors below 10% and over 90% of points within 5% error. It reduces total testing loss by 60.3% compared with conventional PINN, demonstrating improved stability and accuracy.

papers.title: Using diffusion models to estimate uncertainties in analytic continuation
papers.abstract: Inverse problems are ubiquitous in physics, chemistry, and engineering, arising when reconstructing hidden quantities from indirect measurements. A key example is the analytic continuation of imaginary-time correlation functions (iTCFs) to the real-frequency domain. This process requires an inverse Laplace transform, which is numerically ill-posed and highly sensitive to small input variations. Recent neural network (NN)-based methods have shown promising results by learning mappings from imaginary-time to real-frequency spectra, often outperforming traditional techniques such as maximum entropy. However, because the forward transform is strongly smoothing, many spectra can fit the same iTCF. Regression-based approaches output a single spectrum, which approximates an average over the true solution space, and therefore fail to capture the full distribution of plausible power spectra. To address this issue, we introduce a diffusion-based framework for analytic continuation that learns the distribution of spectra consistent with a given iTCF. It offers two key advantages. First, it quantifies uncertainty directly from the learned distribution. Second, by analyzing the spread and structure of this distribution, we can quantitatively assess the intrinsic hardness of each inversion problem. We measure this hardness with a new metric, the uncertainty pseudo-volume. Applying the framework to an iTCF from a path-integral molecular dynamics simulation of liquid parahydrogen, we obtain the self-diffusion coefficient with an error bar and flag a secondary high-frequency peak as a possible spurious artifact. In contrast to previous attempts at uncertainty quantification, our generative approach provides an explicit distribution of spectra conditioned on the input, from which the uncertainty follows directly.

papers.title: ISEFlow: a flow-based neural network emulator for improved sea level projections and uncertainty quantification
papers.abstract: Ice sheets are the primary contributors to global sea level rise, yet projecting their future contributions remains challenging due to the complex, nonlinear processes governing their dynamics and uncertainties in future climate scenarios. This study introduces ISEFlow, a neural network-based emulator of the ISMIP6 ice sheet model ensemble designed to accurately and efficiently emulate sea level contributions from both ice sheets while quantifying the sources of projection uncertainty. By integrating a normalizing flow architecture to capture data coverage uncertainty and a deep ensemble of recurrent neural network models to assess emulator uncertainty, ISEFlow separates uncertainties arising from training data from those inherent to the emulator. Compared to existing emulators such as a Gaussian Process-based emulator modeled after emulandice and LARMIP, ISEFlow achieves substantially lower mean squared error and improved distribution approximation while maintaining faster prediction times. This study investigates the drivers of increased emulation accuracy and emission scenario distinction and finds that the inclusion of all available climate forcings, ice sheet model characteristics, and higher spatial resolution significantly enhances emulation accuracy and the ability to capture the effects of varying emissions scenarios compared to other emulators. We include a detailed analysis of the importance of input variables using Shapley Additive Explanations, and highlight which climate forcings and model characteristics have the largest impact on sea level projections. ISEFlow offers an additional tool for efficient, accurate exploration of future sea level projections.

papers.title: Hierarchical heterostructure engineering for strength–ductility synergy in additively manufactured high-entropy alloys
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing creates high-entropy alloys under thermal conditions that are difficult to reproduce by conventional routes. Rapid solidification, directional heat flow, and repeated reheating generate cellular substructures, melt-pool boundaries, solute-partitioned interfaces, metastable phases, and nanoscale precipitates. These features are often treated separately, although their mechanical effect depends on how they interact across length scales. This Mini Review examines additive manufacturing as a route for constructing hierarchical heterostructures that coordinate strength and plasticity. Emphasis is placed on the conversion of solidification-derived heterogeneity into useful deformation architecture rather than on a process-by-process comparison. Cellular and subgrain structures, lamellar eutectics, coherent or semi-coherent precipitates, metastable phase transformation, ceramic reinforcement, and post-processing are discussed as connected design tools. Recent studies on laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) and directed energy deposition (DED) show that high strength can coexist with substantial tensile ductility when hard regions carry load while softer or transformable regions maintain strain accommodation and when interfaces delay rather than trigger localization. The key challenge is therefore not simply maximizing phase complexity or defect-free density, but controlling the spatial continuity, stability, and mechanical contrast of heterogeneities. Design principles and remaining limitations for microstructure-oriented development of additively manufactured high-entropy alloys are summarized.

papers.abstract: This study examined indications that active learning methods may support learning recovery in eighth-grade science at Centro Educacional Weber Eider in Laranjal do Jari, Amapá, Brazil. The descriptive study combined qualitative and quantitative data and followed the Rediscovering Science project from February to June 2025. The class had 30 enrolled students. Targeted support prioritized those with the greatest observed learning difficulties. Data sources included participant observation, reflective records, a semi-structured interview with the classroom teacher, spontaneous student accounts, and the class’s grades averaged by academic term. The intervention involved dialogic lessons, group discussions, contextualized hands-on activities, a formative quiz, and audiovisual materials. The records indicated greater participation and confidence during the activities. The class average rose from 7.12 to 8.13 in the first semester. In later terms, it fell to 7.22 and then rose to 7.58. The findings describe signs of engagement during the project. Fluctuations in grades and the lack of comparable skillspecific measures limit conclusions about learning recovery and whether the outcomes can be attributed to the intervention.

papers.title: Infrared Thermography With Uncertainty Quantification for High‐Temperature Surface Measurement Through a Flame
papers.abstract: Noninvasive infrared radiation–based temperature measurements are used in many engineering applications. One example is using an infrared (IR) camera to observe a gas turbine combustor liner through a flame and combustion gases and provide its inner‐surface temperature distribution. Imaging through a flame poses many challenges, and thus this study aims at providing detailed procedures to accurately measure the temperature of a metal surface through a flame. Three types of narrow bandpass filters are examined in order to maximize optical transmission through the flame and combustion gases. By using a blackbody furnace, reference temperature measurements and their respective uncertainties were obtained first without a flame and then through a flame. Next, a thin Inconel 718 plate was heated using two butane torches, and the temperature of the plate surface was measured through the flame. The surface temperature was validated using a thermocouple attached to the back of the plate. For the three independently tested spectral bands, the measured plate temperatures were in the range of approximately 1070 K–1120 K. Wavelength‐dependent differences were observed, with the 3915 nm configuration showing the closest agreement with the corrected thermocouple‐based surface temperature. Independent shortwave and midwave infrared measurements were compared across the three spectral bands to identify the wavelength range most suitable for through‐flame thermography. The selection of optical bandpass filters and the uncertainty analysis presented in this study provide a practical basis for high‐temperature surface measurements through a flame.

papers.title: Therapy Performance Predicts Functional Recovery After Stroke
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early prediction of post-stroke recovery is important for guiding personalized rehabilitation and optimizing care planning. However, existing prediction approaches often overlook therapy intensity and patient engagement during post-stroke rehabilitation. OBJECTIVE: Deriving therapy performance metrics (TPMs) from clinical notes and evaluate their utility in predicting functional discharge outcomes on the 10-Meter Walk Test (10MWT), 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), and Berg Balance Scale (BBS). METHODS: Electronic medical records from 42 individuals undergoing inpatient stroke rehabilitation were mined to extract TPMs describing therapy exposure, walking distance, treadmill use, and stair practice. TPMs were evaluated across inpatient time-points to compare distributions between participants who met or did not meet established clinical thresholds for each functional outcome and to assess associations with discharge scores. TPMs were integrated into machine learning (ML) models along with patient demographics and sensor-derived gait features collected at IRF admission. RESULTS: increased from .30 to .63, reduced prediction error by ~25 m) relative to baseline models without TPMs. Importantly, ML models using TPMs enabled early outcome prediction for non-ambulatory patients, a group often excluded from gait-based predictive approaches. CONCLUSION: TPMs provide early markers of recovery and enhance the prediction of discharge outcomes, particularly for patients who are non-ambulatory at admission. Leveraging structured information from routine therapy documentation may enable dynamic, near real-time recovery prediction to support data-driven rehabilitation and care planning after stroke.

papers.title: Nationwide mapping of mangrove EWT and LMA in China using universal sensitive subdomains and Bayesian-optimized machine learning models
papers.abstract: Mangroves support global carbon cycling and biodiversity. Leaf equivalent water thickness (EWT) and leaf mass per area (LMA), core functional traits, are vital ecological monitoring indicators. Yet vague spectral response mechanisms hamper precise, stable large-scale remote sensing inversion. This study constructed a national sensitive spectral screening framework based on 1023 plots and 102,300 full-spectrum field data across China’s mangrove zones. Combining spectral clustering and cross-regional meta-analysis, we used group-differential gradient perturbation two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy (GDGP-2D-COS) and Bayesian optimization to extract sensitive bands and identify regional optimal wavelengths and universal sensitive subdomains. We further developed 120 inversion strategies to generate high-resolution national maps of mangrove EWT and LMA across China. Our results reveal universal sensitive subdomains cover 795–878 nm, 968–975 nm, 1735–1765 nm, and 2021–2050 nm; LMA lies in the red edge and SWIR regions: 729–765 nm, 1564–1672 nm, and 1978–1990 nm. Four machine-learning verifications prove that regional and universal bands yield robust accuracy: EWT R 2 = 0.620–0.965, LMA R 2 = 0.504–0.908. Tested on Sentinel-2 and ZY-1 02E data, universal sensitive spectral subdomains remain steady (EWT R 2 = 0.506–0.965; LMA R 2 = 0.444–0.848). China’s mangrove EWT is 0.205–0.550 kg/m2 and LMA 0.06–0.214 kg/m2, matching ecological benchmarks. This work supplies scientific and technical support for mangrove carbon sink assessment, targeted ecosystem management and sustainable conservation.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Prediction of 3D Printability of Microgel-Based Bioink
papers.abstract: High-fidelity 3D bioprinting is essential for producing biomimetic tissue scaffolds for precision medicine. A core challenge arises from the strong nonlinear coupling between microgel viscoelasticity and printing parameters, which governs shape fidelity. Conventional trial-and-error optimization is low-efficiency and fails to quantify these complex relationships. Herein, we developed a data-driven framework for predicting microgel printability using a model microgel composed of gelatin methacrylate and a small-molecule crosslinker with tunable crosslinking densities, sizes, and rheological properties. A multidimensional evaluation system was established to annotate printing outcomes, generating a high-throughput dataset linking viscoelastic properties to process parameters. Of the seven machine learning models evaluated, the multilayer perceptron achieved the highest test accuracy of 79.18%. The optimized model enables accurate prediction across diverse material compositions, geometric patterns, and cell-laden bioinks. This work represents the first data-driven model for printability prediction of microgel-based bioinks, affording a theoretical basis for the reverse design of tailored microgel formulations and optimal process windows.

papers.title: Investigating Surfactant-Induced Modulation of Electron–Hole Mobility Asymmetry in Graphene/hBN Heterostructures
papers.abstract: In this work, noncovalent surfactants (sodium octyl sulfate and sodium cholate) functionalization is demonstrated as an effective and reproducible strategy for engineering carrier-selective transport in graphene/hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) heterostructures. Temperature-dependent electrical measurements revealed that sodium octyl sulfate (SOS) promotes electron-dominated conduction, whereas sodium cholate (SC) induces hole-selective transport. These opposite transport behaviors were consistently observed across multiple devices and were quantitatively confirmed through normalized mobility asymmetry factors and mobility ratio analyses. The results indicate that surfactant adsorption modifies carrier scattering, electrostatic screening, and charge-transfer interactions at the graphene interface, leading to distinct electron–hole transport asymmetries. The persistence of these effects over the investigated temperature range indicates that the observed carrier selectivity originates from stable interfacial interactions rather than thermal fluctuations. Furthermore, the magnitude of the transport asymmetry exceeded device-to-device variability, indicating that it originates from surfactant adsorption rather than from fabrication-related variability. The findings establish molecular functionalization as a scalable, solution-based approach for tuning charge transport symmetry in graphene-enabled devices without significantly disrupting their lattice structure. This capability provides new opportunities for optimizing graphene-based electronics, sensors, and low-power devices. Furthermore, the asymmetry analysis framework developed in this work provides a quantitative basis for assessing carrier-selective transport in graphene/hBN devices and may be extended to other van der Waals heterostructures in future work.

papers.abstract: Process safety management in petrochemical facilities remains challenging due to complex operating conditions, equipment degradation, and limitations in conventional monitoring systems. This study proposes a Physics-Informed Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (PI-MARL) framework for supervisory process safety barrier management. The architecture integrates physics-informed neural networks, cooperative learning agents, equipment reliability assessment, and safety-constrained decision support. A continuous stirred-tank reactor is selected as the representative process for a proposed simulation-based evaluation involving operating disturbances, equipment degradation, and impaired protective barriers. The framework incorporates physical governing equations, safety-aware reward functions, and supervisory action screening while maintaining the independence of established safety instrumented systems. The evaluation protocol specifies comparisons with conventional control, model predictive control, and safe reinforcement learning methods using safety violations, barrier availability, prediction errors, and computational performance. The study establishes a conceptual and mathematical foundation for evaluating coordinated, risk-informed supervisory decisions. Experimental validation is required to determine its effectiveness and practical applicability.

papers.abstract: On 18 November 2026, Randall Balestriero, Yann LeCun and Kerda Varaku submitted a paper to arXiv (2611.24778). It shows how a frozen world model can answer "what would have happened if I had chosen differently?". It takes a small step on the action and reads the difference in the model's predictions, with no retraining. An Indian technical note was posted ahead of this paper by one of the world's best-known AI researchers. The author's Zenodo note of 4 November 2026, 14 days earlier, took a small step on the settings of a frozen AI model itself. The settings are the non-learned ones, and the input is unchanged. The spread of the scores shows how firm the score is. A wide spread starts a shunting action: the computer decides without waiting for a person, and it moves the work aside instead of stopping it. The two works ask different questions: "what if?" and "how firm?". This note puts them side by side, with dates and DOIs, and explains how the firmness reading differs from Bayesian networks and Monte Carlo dropout.

papers.abstract: Near-hull inspection requires the tracking of a prescribed path while maintaining clearance from structural hazards. This numerical study combines geometry-based reference generation with nonlinear model predictive control. The controller adjusts the steering increment penalty according to position uncertainty and uses a Gaussian inequality to limit the summed hazard field at predicted positions. In the corrected five-path nominal tests, the original capture-gated controller and its matched-reference fixed-weight counterpart achieved mean original-path lateral RMSEs of 0.10625 and 0.10606m and mean minimum clearances of 0.39310 and 0.39060m, respectively. Scheduling reduced the noisy-segment steering rate RMS by 48.5% relative to the low-noise constant and reduced the low-noise curved-segment RMSE by 44.0% relative to the high-noise constant. The tracking error and fallback frequency increased relative to the low-noise constant, indicating a scenario-dependent trade-off. A global upper bound showed that geometric clearance alone kept the Gaussian field below its limit in the original separated layouts. In three overlapping layouts, both ablation arms satisfied the sampled clearance requirement, while adding the Gaussian inequality with a predictive margin of 0.008 reduced the peak sampled field intensity from 1.2837–1.3050 to 1.1451–1.1468. The findings apply to the tested numerical scenarios.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Radiographic Identification, Detection, and Prediction of Complications Post-Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Background/Objective: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been investigated for the radiographic recognition of existing complications and prediction of subsequent adverse outcomes after total hip arthroplasty (THA). We synthesized the reported diagnostic and prognostic performance and examined testing strategies, calibration, and methodological limitations. Methods: We conducted a systematic review reported in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020. Eligible English-language full-text studies published between 1 January 2010 and 31 August 2026, evaluated Artificial intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML) models using radiographic information, alone or with clinical data, to detect an existing post-THA complication or predict a subsequent complication or implant failure. Mixed-population studies required separately extractable THA-specific results. The final search was executed on 21 October 2026. Eligible models incorporated radiographic images or image-derived features; clinical-only models were not eligible. A structured narrative synthesis was used because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Results: Twelve studies met the eligibility criteria for qualitative synthesis after the exclusion of studies focused on pre-arthroplasty osteoarthritis progression or short-term need for THA, which were outside the pre-defined review scope. Across the included post-THA studies, AI models were applied to tasks including aseptic loosening detection, multiclass failure classification, dislocation risk prediction, periprosthetic fracture as a label within the broader THA complication recognition, and longitudinal prediction of prosthesis failure. Several studies reported high apparent discrimination, particularly in internally validated single-center datasets, while some studies evaluated performance in additional institutional cohorts. Registry linkage was not treated as evidence of external evaluation. However, the evidence base was limited by substantial heterogeneity in populations, outcome definitions, model designs, and validation strategies, and most studies were judged to be at high overall risk of bias. Conclusions: Current evidence suggests that AI-based radiographic assessment of selected post-THA complications is promising, but the principal limitations are incomplete independent external evaluation, sparse calibration and clinical-utility evidence, and methodological concerns. The reported retrospective performance does not establish improved implant survivorship or patient outcomes. A prospective multicenter evaluation, transparent reporting, human–AI workflow assessment, and clinical-impact studies are needed before routine adoption.

papers.title: Hybrid Optimization for Hydrological Modeling and Runoff Partitioning in the Xiangjiang River Basin
papers.abstract: Reliable hydrological model calibration is essential for assessing long-term runoff variability. This study developed a sequential Bayesian optimization-shuffled complex evolution (BO-SCE-UA) framework to calibrate the Variable Infiltration Capacity (VIC) model and investigate runoff variability and partitioning in China’s Xiangjiang River Basin during 1959–2024. The hybrid framework achieved a Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.85, compared with 0.84 and 0.83 for standalone BO and SCE-UA, respectively. The calibrated model reproduced observed discharge at daily, monthly, and annual timescales. More than 69.9% of annual discharge occurred during April–September. Annual discharge at Xiangtan Station showed no significant long-term trend (p = 0.438). Although positive Sen’s slope estimates were found in 75.02% of the basin grid cells, none of the annual runoff-depth trends remained statistically significant after Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction (q < 0.05). Surface runoff and baseflow contributed 54.49% and 45.51% of mean annual total runoff, respectively. Surface runoff exceeded baseflow during most months, except July and December. Neither runoff component nor the annual baseflow index showed a significant long-term trend. Baseflow contributions were relatively high in the northern and eastern basin. These findings characterize long-term runoff variability and partitioning using a consistently calibrated distributed hydrological model.

papers.title: Learning-Based Tube Model Predictive Control for Mixed Vehicle Platoons with Uncertainty-Aware Trajectory Prediction
papers.abstract: In mixed platoons, CAVs cannot communicate with the HDV leaders they follow and thus must rely on prediction models to estimate their future trajectories. The resulting prediction errors, if left untreated, can severely degrade the car-following performance of downstream CAVs under conventional MPC. To counter this, we develop a learning-based Tube MPC framework that explicitly incorporates HDV trajectory uncertainty into robust control design. Specifically, a deep learning predictor supplies nominal HDV motions, while a state-innovation scheme converts the real-time prediction residuals into equivalent disturbances that directly enter the relative-state dynamics. Instead of relying on fixed, over-conservative disturbance bounds, we online learn a compact quantified disturbance set from these collected realizations, which dynamically adapts the tube size for MPC constraint tightening. Simulations on a five-vehicle platoon demonstrate that the learned set successfully shrinks the tube while preserving robust constraint satisfaction. Compared with CACC, nominal MPC, and fixed Tube MPC baselines, our method significantly reduces spacing and relative velocity errors, demonstrating improved tracking accuracy under prediction uncertainty, although a trade-off between tracking accuracy and control smoothness remains.

papers.title: Physics-guided curve-residual deep learning for within-domain permeability prediction of calcareous-sand concrete
papers.abstract: Introduction Permeability affects the durability of calcareous-sand concrete under pressure loading. Its dependence on composition, pore pressure, confining pressure, and loading history is difficult to characterize from limited pressure-sweep data. This study developed a physics-guided framework to complete partly measured pressure curves within the experimental domain. Methods The dataset comprised 462 gas-permeability measurements from 77 six-point pressure curves. The physics-conditioned curve-residual deep neural network (PCR-DNN) combined physically motivated input features, weak directional regularization, and curve calibration based on training observations. We evaluated performance using a pressure-point split and a separate whole-curve holdout. Benchmarks included a deep neural network (DNN), a physics-guided deep neural network (PG-DNN), support vector regression (SVR), Gaussian process regression (GPR), CatBoost, and direct interpolation. Results With four measurements available from the same curve, PCR-DNN achieved a test R 2 of 0.9937 for the withheld pressure point. Linear and natural cubic-spline interpolation achieved R 2 values of 0.9987 and 0.9990, respectively, on the same task. In the whole-curve holdout, the log-scale R 2 values for DNN, PG-DNN, and CatBoost ranged from 0.9178 to 0.9523; those for SVR and GPR were 0.9065 and 0.9270, respectively. Discussion Direct interpolation is suitable for completing an individual measured curve. PCR-DNN provides a common model for within-domain prediction and consistency checks across the recorded experimental conditions. Its curve-completion accuracy applies when measurements from the target curve are available for calibration.

papers.title: Learning Flexible Correlations in Gaussian Processes for Structured Categorical Inputs
papers.abstract: Gaussian process (GP) models are widely used for prediction and uncertainty quantification in computer experiments and scientific applications. However, most mixed-input GP methods treat categorical variables as flat factors, ignoring the grouped or hierarchical organization that frequently arises in practice. We propose the Unrestrictive Correlation Gaussian Process Model for Grouped Factors (UC-Grouped), a flexible kernel construction for mixed inputs with structured categorical factors. UC-Grouped decomposes categorical dependence into two interpretable components: a correlation matrix across groups and block-diagonal correlation matrices for levels within groups. These components are combined through a positive semidefinite convex mixture with a learnable weight, allowing the model to adaptively balance cross-group similarity and within-group heterogeneity. Both correlation layers are parameterized using a hyperspherical construction that guarantees valid correlation matrices while enabling rich, nonexchangeable dependence patterns. Across controlled simulation studies, UC-Grouped often achieves the best predictive, interval, and scoring-rule performance, with its clearest gains when both group-level and within-group level effects are present. A real application to airfoil self-noise data shows that UC-Grouped gives the best average predictive and scoring-rule performance among the structured GP models compared, while providing interpretable estimates of relationships among frequency regimes and angle levels. Although more computationally demanding than simpler GP alternatives, UC-Grouped offers a principled and general framework for hierarchical categorical inputs. By balancing flexibility, interpretability, and predictive performance, the proposed method broadens the applicability of GPs to modern computer experiments and complex applied statistical problems.

papers.abstract: Advanced practice registered nurses require pharmacological competence across all populations to provide safe and effective care. Advanced practice registered nurse students report feeling under-prepared to manage vulnerable populations, including pregnant or lactating patients, older adults, and patients on multiple medications, based on traditional lecture-based pharmacology education alone. papers.title: From Viewing to Learning: Reimagining Subtitled Films as Catalysts for English Language Development
papers.abstract: Subtitled films have emerged as a valuable multimedia resource for supporting English language learning among English as a Second Language (ESL) learners. Unlike traditional instructional approaches that rely primarily on textbooks and classroom interaction, subtitled films combine visual and auditory input to create meaningful and authentic language-learning experiences. Guided by Dual Coding Theory and Multimedia Learning Theory, this paper examines how subtitled films contribute to English language development through four interconnected dimensions: motivation and learner engagement, vocabulary acquisition and retention, pronunciation and listening development, and multimodal communication competence. The discussion highlights that subtitles support language learning by providing contextualised vocabulary exposure, authentic pronunciation models, repeated listening opportunities, and increased learner autonomy. Furthermore, digital platforms such as Netflix create flexible self-learning environments that enable students to engage with English beyond formal classroom instruction. The paper also argues that subtitled films promote active learning by reducing language anxiety and increasing students' willingness to participate in communication activities. While the benefits of subtitled media are substantial, the discussion emphasises the importance of integrating film-based learning within broader pedagogical strategies that encourage reflection, practice, and meaningful communication. Future research should examine interactive subtitles, artificial intelligence-enhanced media learning, long-term vocabulary retention, and the effectiveness of subtitled films across different proficiency levels and educational contexts.

papers.title: Data‐Driven Composition Discovery in Rutile IrO 2 ‐Based Mixed‐Metal Oxides for Enhanced Oxygen Evolution Catalysis
papers.abstract: Identifying an active and acid‐stable oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalyst remains a primary challenge for proton exchange membrane electrolyzers. Here, we combine design of experiments (DoE), machine learning (ML), and theoretical activity calculations to identify multi‐component platinum group metal oxide‐based OER catalysts in acidic media. A DoE exploration of the Ir–Pt–Pd–Os composition space trained a Gaussian process regression ML model, which ranked predicted overpotentials for 1771 compositions. Active learning identified an optimal Ir‐rich compositional region (60%–70% Ir, 15%–35% Pt, ≤10% Pd and Os), represented by Ir 0.65 Pt 0.20 Pd 0.10 Os 0.05 oxide and Ir 0.65 Pt 0.35 oxide, which outperform rutile IrO 2. We experimentally confirmed that both oxides deliver a two to threefold gain in Ir‐mass activity over amorphous IrO x at 1.55 V vs. RHE. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that only Pt mixes into rutile IrO 2 beyond trace levels, establishing that dopant miscibility is set by oxo‐compatibility. At the surface, charge withdrawal by the less oxophilic Pd and Pt dopants raises the oxidation states of neighboring Ir sites, consistent with x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy results, whereas Os does the opposite. These more oxidized Ir sites are also predicted to be more active for OER. This integrated computational–experimental workflow accelerates catalyst discovery in complex compositional spaces.

papers.title: Predicting the Impact Sensitivity of Energetic Materials From Small Datasets: A Multi‐Task Graph Neural Network Approach Utilizing Co‐Measured Properties
papers.abstract: Impact sensitivity is a vital safety metric of energetic materials whose measurement is expensive and dangerous, with public datasets limited to hundreds of molecules. Using the 307‐molecule Mathieu dataset under a leakage‐free nested cross‐validation framework (outer five‐fold; molecule‐level inner split; four seeds averaged), this work asks whether MPNN surpasses descriptor‐based machine learning and at which data size, whether co‐training with co‐measured density, detonation velocity and pressure helps without extra computed data, and how to quantify applicability domain and predictive uncertainty. The single‐task MPNN (R 2 = 0.616 ± 0.030) matches or slightly exceeds the strongest descriptor baseline, gradient boosting (0.571 ± 0.104); its clearest advantage is data efficiency, outperforming the random forest from 50% of the data upward (crossover between 25% and 50%). Four‐task co‐training (R 2 = 0.653 ± 0.018) shows a small fold‐level gain (Δ R 2 = +0.037, p = 0.028) not confirmed at the molecule level, while all co‐measured auxiliary properties are predicted accurately (R 2 ≈ 0.95); the detonation‐velocity configuration shows the highest mean performance among tested auxiliary tasks. External validation on the 537‐molecule Marrs dataset reveals large extrapolation errors dominated by inconsistent experimental protocols, with reliability conditional on the training domain (Mathieu‐type CHNO molecules, 2.5 kg drop‐weight protocol) and lower for compounds from different protocols or under‐represented structural classes. Conformal‐calibrated deep‐ensemble intervals reach the nominal coverage. This work offers rigorous evidence for small‐sample energetic‐material modelling: graph‐representation data efficiency, multi‐task value as zero‐cost regularization, and operational applicability‐domain and uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: Review of Additive Aluminium Matrix Composite Materials: Processing, Microstructure, Mechanical Properties and Defects
papers.abstract: In response to rigorous lightweighting requirements, material development has increasingly concentrated on high strength-to-weight ratio systems that can provide superior mechanical properties without compromising durability. High-performance, lightweight aluminium (Al) composite materials have emerged as a cornerstone solution, valued for their exceptional specific strength, specific stiffness, tailorable properties, and corrosion resistance. This review paper examines the processing of additive aluminium metal matrix composites (AMMCs) via laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) and direct energy deposition (DED). It explores the effects of both in situ and ex situ conditions during processing. The review evaluates the outcomes of each process and the influence of process parameters on the resulting aluminium matrix composites (AMCs) and various reinforcements employed to enhance mechanical properties. Additionally, it investigates the microstructure produced by each method, reinforcement used and its correlation with the mechanical properties obtained. The review also discusses the primary defect mechanisms associated with LPBF and DED, including porosity, lack of fusion, keyhole defects, hot cracking, and anisotropy. Furthermore, it highlights recent advancements in process optimization, reinforcement-assisted defect suppression, and defect characterization.

papers.title: RiskPath-PV: risk-aware adaptive UAV path planning for automated inspection of photovoltaic arrays
papers.abstract: Defects in large photovoltaic (PV) farms are spatially sparse, and battery limited unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) cannot scan full areas. RiskPath-PV is an adaptive UAV inspection path planning framework that uses PV string operational information as a defect risk prior. A string topology graph turns telemetry into a module level risk field trained on a perturbed surrogate of inspection regret rather than detection accuracy, weighted non exchangeable conformal risk control converts a target miss rate of critical defects into a coverage constraint, and a consistency gate binds the reinforcement learning policy to a greedy policy with an adaptive submodular guarantee, while replanning is limited to rounds bound to battery swap windows. Models were trained on two operating plants and tested on a third, unseen plant in four seasonal missions; the plants range from 50 to 210 MW, and module level ground truth came from handheld infrared and electroluminescence campaigns. All budget-constrained planners flew the same aircraft under an energy cap of 30% of full coverage, and recall was counted against the defects confirmed by full coverage. Under this cap, the proposed method reached a mean recall of 86.8%, 8.6 percentage points above an energy aware planner guided by maximum power point anomalies, with a gain in every season, and reduced flight time by 12.3%. At a nominal miss rate of 0.05, the measured critical miss rate was 0.049, and recall retention reached 96.4% at 4.2 times the training scale. Ablation showed that decision focused training contributed 5.7 points of recall, the conformal layer held critical misses below 5% (12.4% without it), limited round replanning produced the flight time saving (the full 13.2 kWh cap without it), and the coordinate free encoding and the gate sustained scale transfer (85.3% and 89.2% retention without them).

papers.title: Contrasting Live Case Studies and Challenge-Based Learning in Operations Management Education: An Exploratory Integrative Framework
papers.abstract: Operations Management (OM) higher education faces a persistent paradox: despite being an inherently practice-oriented discipline, instruction frequently relies on static, lecture-based textbook cases. Furthermore, realistic, stakeholder-linked active learning approaches, pedagogical comparisons, and alignment with authentic assessment principles are scarce in the literature. To address this gap, this study compares two experiential pedagogical approaches, live case studies (LCS) and challenge-based learning (CBL), to examine how their distinct designs support active learning, authentic assessment, and institutional feasibility. Adopting a qualitative, exploratory multiple-case design structured by the ADDIE instructional model, this study examines a Level 6 undergraduate module using LCS and a Level 7 executive MBA module using CBL within British higher education. The ADDIE-guided comparison of instructional designs drew on module documentation, illustrative teaching examples, and descriptive assessment and evaluation results. The study identified differences in problem framing, stakeholder integration, competency focus, assessment design, and institutional requirements. Undergraduate LCS emphasised student-defined operational problems and analytical tools, whereas postgraduate CBL centred on a shared simulated challenge involving systems thinking and competing stakeholder perspectives. The cases illustrated different facilitation and coordination arrangements, although broader scalability remains to be determined. The primary limitation of this study is its comparison of two modules within a single institution, underscoring the need for future longitudinal research across broader educational settings. Ultimately, this study advances a context-sensitive framework that reframes active OM pedagogy as a configurable design space, offering educators guidance on aligning authentic assessment with student profiles, learning goals, and institutional constraints.

papers.abstract: Physical layer authentication is a key enabling technology for endogenous security in 5G/6G networks. However, radio frequency fingerprinting (RFF) faces bottlenecks in vertical industry deployments such as the power Internet of Things (IoT), including extremely small differences among same-batch devices and scarce labeled samples. This paper proposes a bispectrum-guided active learning method with discrepancy enhancement for RFF identification, validated on ZigBee terminals in power systems to achieve reliable device identity authentication under limited labeling. First, a dual-branch gated fusion network is constructed, which takes square integral bispectrum (SIB) as the primary feature and short-time Fourier transform (STFT) time–frequency representation as auxiliary information, adaptively fusing the two complementary features to enhance subtle discrepancy representation among same-model devices. Second, a bispectrum-guided active learning sampling strategy is designed, which uses bispectrum hardware similarity to dynamically identify boundary device pairs and prioritize samples with the highest discriminative value; a hardware-similarity-weighted contrastive loss is introduced to focus the model on difficult device pairs with high hardware similarity. On this basis, a class-specific distance modeling method based on extreme value theory is introduced to achieve integrated unknown device detection and identity authentication. Experiments on a dataset of 20 same-model ZigBee devices show that the inter-class to intra-class distance ratio of SIB features is 40.8% higher than that of STFT; active learning requires only about 8.3% of labeled samples to approach fully supervised performance; and in open-set recognition, the composite detection metric for unknown devices reaches 0.89 (on a scale of 1), outperforming the compared methods. The results demonstrate clear advantages in labeling efficiency, same-model device discrimination, and open-set security.

papers.abstract: Relational Dynamics™: Theory of System Trajectories · Research Architecture Overview · v0.1 关系动力学™:系统轨迹理论 · 研究架构概览 · v0.1 A Versioned Overview of an Evolving Research Programme 持续发展中的研究体系:一份版本化架构概览 This research architecture note presents a versioned overview of Relational Dynamics™: Theory of System Trajectories (关系动力学™:系统轨迹理论), an original and evolving theoretical framework developed by Alice Jing Shan 单景. Taking the system trajectory as its primary unit of analysis, the theory examines how systems form, stabilise, drift, adapt, transform, and potentially collapse. Its philosophical foundation is articulated through the Ontology of Relational Dynamics, with the central proposition: Reality is relational dynamics under constraint over time. The document outlines three interconnected levels of inquiry: Upstream — Ontological Foundation: the philosophical orientation informing the wider research programme. Midstream — Epistemology, Methodology, and Analytical Models: ten selected research components, including System Trajectory Modelling, The Five Human Systems, System Stability Matrix, the Excellence–Capacity–Coherence Model (ECC), Survivable Risk Window (SRW), Linguistic Seam Analysis (LSA), the Relational Dynamics™ Interface Audit Framework, the Relational Dynamics™ Field Model (RDFM), the Mortise-Tenon Cube Lattice Structure Model, and Dao Models of Mutual Generation. Downstream — Research and Professional Practice: cross-domain systems research, second-order structural analysis, and Advisor to Advisors (A2A), together with seventeen selected research themes and application domains. The architecture distinguishes between independent development of original theory and methodology at the upstream and midstream levels, and open research and professional collaboration at the downstream level. The downstream provides an interface through which the theoretical and analytical resources of Relational Dynamics™ can be brought into dialogue with the situated knowledge, expertise, and practical experience of domain specialists. The architecture emphasises an iterative relationship between theoretical development, methodological inquiry, and practical engagement: The theory provides the architecture; practice provides its real-world stress test. Practice feedback primarily informs midstream methodological and analytical development, while upstream philosophical assumptions remain open to critical examination when warranted. This document records the research architecture as presented on 23 November 2026. It is not an exhaustive catalogue of the research programme, nor does it claim comprehensive empirical validation. Some components remain under development, while others are presented without their full operational specifications. The purpose of this publication is to establish a public, versioned, and traceable reference point for subsequent theoretical development, methodological clarification, interdisciplinary dialogue, professional collaboration, and critical examination. Traceability is part of the method. Stable ontology. papers.title: Peningkatan Akurasi Deteksi Berita Palsu melalui Optimasi Parameter Model Random Forest
papers.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengevaluasi pengaruh optimasi parameter terhadap akurasi algoritma Random Forest dalam mendeteksi berita palsu. Data yang digunakan merupakan dataset sekunder dari platform Kaggle, berisi lebih dari 23.000 entri teks dengan label klasifikasi real dan fake. Metode yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini adalah kuantitatif dengan pendekatan perbandingan performa model sebelum dan sesudah tuning parameter. Proses praproses teks dilakukan melalui tahapan case folding, penghapusan karakter khusus dan stopwords, serta stemming menggunakan pustaka Sastrawi. Optimasi parameter dilakukan menggunakan teknik GridSearchCV terhadap parameter n_estimators, max_depth, dan min_samples_split. Evaluasi model dilakukan dengan menggunakan metrik akurasi, presisi, recall, dan skor F1. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa model yang telah dioptimasi mengalami peningkatan akurasi dari 78,5% menjadi 82%, serta peningkatan nilai presisi, recall, dan skor F1. Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa tuning parameter pada algoritma Random Forest mampu meningkatkan performa klasifikasi dalam konteks deteksi berita palsu. Penelitian ini diharapkan dapat menjadi dasar pengembangan sistem deteksi otomatis yang lebih akurat dan efisien. Penelitian selanjutnya disarankan untuk mengeksplorasi metode tuning lain seperti RandomizedSearchCV atau Bayesian Optimization serta menerapkan pendekatan yang sama pada algoritma pembelajaran mesin lainnya.

papers.title: A Physics Informed Neural Network framework for solving time fractional Navier–Stokes equations
papers.abstract: The Navier–Stokes equations are a system of nonlinear partial differential equations that govern the dynamics of incompressible fluid flows and are widely used in fluid mechanics, heat transfer, aerodynamics, and various engineering applications. This study investigates the time-fractional Navier–Stokes equations (TFNSE) in cylindrical coordinates through the Modified Laplace Adomian Decomposition Method (MLADM) and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) approach. The PINN framework employs a fully connected deep multilayer perceptron (MLP) with multiple hidden layers and the $$tanh (\cdot )$$ activation function. Depending on the numerical example, appropriate network architectures, learning rates, and collocation-point distributions are selected through preliminary numerical tuning to ensure stable and accurate training. The proposed methodologies are employed to obtain accurate approximate solutions of the considered fractional fluid flow model. A comparative analysis is carried out with existing results available in the literature to validate the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed approaches. Numerical simulations, graphical visualizations are presented to examine the effect of the fractional parameter on the solution behaviour. The study demonstrates that the PINN framework provides accurate and computationally efficient approximations, while the MLADM solution serves as the numerical benchmark for validating the PINN results.

papers.title: A stochastic energy-carbon decomposition framework for steelmaking: Integrating LMDI and Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Gas-based steelmaking depends on both electricity and natural gas. Traditional methods usually combine these sources and use fixed estimates that do not account for uncertainty. This study introduces a new framework that applies fuel-specific Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) analysis with Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification, extends the Generalized Divisia Index Method (GDIM) for CO₂ emission analysis, and includes scenario-based assessments. Applied to Iran's DRI-EAF-focused steel industry from 2016 to 2023, the framework separates electricity and natural gas use for blast-furnace and electric-arc-furnace routes, highlighting their different energy profiles. The findings show that electricity use increased by 57.7% (13,708 million kWh) and natural gas use by 75.1% (6642 million m³), mainly because steel output rose by 73%. Monte Carlo simulations with 10,000 runs confirm that the activity-level effect is consistently positive (95% CI: [13,547–18,419] million kWh; CV = 7.8%). However, the uncertainty range for gas intensity includes zero (95% CI: [−1638 to +2328] million m³), so improvements in gas efficiency are not statistically clear, which deterministic analyses do not show. The GDIM extension finds that CO₂ emissions increased by 19.69 Mt, with natural gas responsible for 66% of this rise. Scenario analysis suggests that combining policy and technology changes could save 52,960 million kWh of electricity and 21,904 million m³ of natural gas compared to business-as-usual. This framework gives decision-makers a practical tool that accounts for uncertainty and helps them prioritize energy-efficiency investments in gas-based steel industries facing supply challenges.

papers.title: Effects of two teacher-led physical activity interventions on academic performance, aerobic fitness, well-being, and school-related motivation in Danish children: the ACTIVE SCHOOL cluster randomised controlled trial
papers.abstract: Background Physical activity may enhance learning, but few studies have compared the effectiveness of different physical activity interventions on academic outcomes. Methods ACTIVE SCHOOL was an eight-month, three-arm cluster randomised controlled trial conducted in Denmark. Third-grade children (age 9–10-years) were randomly assigned at the school-level (1:1:1) to 1) ​ Move & Learn (n = 11 schools, 522 students); 2) ​ Run, Jump, & Fun (n = 11 schools, 540 students); or 3) usual practice (control, n = 11 schools, 365 students). Move & Learn integrated physically active learning into mathematics and Danish language lessons.​ Run, Jump, & Fun provided moderate-to-vigorous intensity activity without integration into the academic content and could be implemented in all academic lessons or in other timeslots during the day. Both interventions aimed to provide four weekly 30-minute physical activity sessions. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in mathematics performance from baseline to follow-up, assessed using standardised age-appropriate computerised tests and analysed using the intention-to-treat principle. Secondary outcomes were Danish language performance, well-being, school-related motivation, and aerobic fitness. Results ACTIVE SCHOOL enrolled 33 schools (n = 1115 children). Mathematics performance data were available for n = 968 children at baseline, n = 740 at follow-up, and n = 661 (59%) at both time-points. Compared with control, the mean difference in change in mathematics performance was 16.6 points (95%CI: 12.1 to 21.1, p < 0.001) for Move & Learn and 7.7 points (95%CI: 3.4 to 12.1, p = 0.001) for Run, Jump, & Fun. Improvement was greater for Move & Learn compared with Run, Jump, & Fun (mean difference: 8.9 points, 95%CI: 5.0 to 12.7, p < 0.001). The improvement in aerobic fitness was greater in Move & Learn compared with Run, Jump, & Fun (mean difference: 30.8 meters, 95%CI: 13.1 to 48.5, p < 0.001). No other between-group differences were observed for secondary outcomes. Conclusion In this cluster randomised controlled trial of 9–10-year-old children, both school-based physical activity interventions improved mathematics performance compared with usual school practice. The intervention with physical activity integrated with academic content produced greater improvements than the intervention with physical activity without integration into the academic content. papers.title: Closed-loop, tooth-to-implant biointerface engineering: dental pulp stem cells at titanium surfaces for cell-enabled osseointegration.
papers.abstract: Dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) and stem cells from human exfoliated deciduous teeth (SHEDs) are underused, tooth-derived regenerative resources with particular relevance to implant dentistry. Routinely extracted third molars, orthodontically removed premolars, and exfoliated deciduous teeth provide recurrent sources of viable pulp tissue that are largely discarded, creating an opportunity to convert surgical waste into a clinically linked regenerative product. This review critically examines how dental pulp-derived cells interact with titanium and titanium-based biomaterials and evaluates their potential for osseointegration and peri-implant bone regeneration. Across the available evidence, these cells adhered to titanium, responded to micro-, nano-, and meso-scale topography, and were modulated by surface chemistry, wettability, ion incorporation, ultraviolet photofunctionalization, plasma treatment, and biofunctional ligands. These interfaces influenced attachment, proliferation, osteogenic differentiation, angiogenic signaling, immunomodulation, antibacterial activity, and mineralized matrix formation. In vivo studies further demonstrated improvements in peri-implant bone formation, bone-implant contact (BIC), trabecular architecture, and early mechanical fixation after DPSC or SHED delivery. Collectively, the available evidence provides preliminary preclinical support for the biological feasibility of engineering dental pulp-derived cell-titanium interfaces but is insufficient to establish clinical readiness. We therefore propose the SEED framework-Source, Expansion, Engineered interface, and Delivery-for closed-loop tooth-to-implant regeneration. SEED leverages the procedural proximity of tooth harvesting to dental care and integrates cell sourcing, clinically compatible expansion, instructive titanium design, and site-specific delivery. Translation remains limited by the small number and heterogeneity of animal studies, short follow-up periods, limited evaluation under functional loading, incomplete information regarding transplanted-cell fate, and frequent reliance on serum-containing culture systems. Future studies will require standardized, clinically compatible and preferably xeno-free processing, application-specific potency testing, longitudinal cell tracking, disease-relevant models, and long-term functional validation under microbial, inflammatory, vascular, and mechanical challenge. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Dental pulp-derived stem cells provide a distinctive opportunity to connect an accessible, frequently discarded biological resource with engineered implant biomaterials. This systematic review integrates evidence from 33 in vitro/ex vivo and four preclinical in vivo studies to determine how titanium topography, physicochemical properties, and biofunctionalization regulate dental pulp-derived cell behavior and implant-related bone regeneration. Beyond evidence synthesis, we identify major material-cell and translational design gaps and introduce the SEED framework-Source, Expansion, Engineered interface, and Delivery-to conceptualize these variables as an integrated regenerative system. The resulting closed-loop tooth-to-implant paradigm reframes titanium from a passive cell carrier into an instructive regenerative interface and provides a biomaterials-centered roadmap for developing cell-enabled strategies for osseointegration.

papers.title: 3D bioprinting of cell-laden alginate and nanocellulose bioinks: characterization and suggestive application for auricle reconstruction.
papers.abstract: The reconstruction of the external auricle remains challenging due to its complex anatomical architecture and the limitations of current surgical approaches. In this study, sodium alginate (SA) and cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) were combined to develop optimized polysaccharide-based bioinks for extrusion 3D bioprinting. Several SA/CNCs formulations were evaluated in terms of rheological behaviour, printability, shape fidelity before and after crosslinking, and preliminary qualitative biological assessment. Ionic crosslinking was performed using 80 mM CaCl₂. Among the tested formulations, the 3% (w/v) SA and 4% (w/v) CNCs bioink showed the best overall performance, with high structural fidelity, a mean area discrepancy of 0.88 mm2 after printing, and 6.49% deformation after crosslinking. The optimized formulation was then used to fabricate an auricle-like scaffold incorporating human dermal fibroblasts. After one week of culture, DAPI staining, Masson's trichrome, Hematoxylin-Eosin staining, and FE-SEM revealed cell-associated structures within and on the scaffold. Additional Ki-67 immunohistochemical analysis showed a small number of positive nuclei in selected regions, suggesting localized cell-cycle activity. However, these qualitative observations do not provide a direct assessment of cell viability or establish the cytocompatibility of the bioink. Therefore, the biological evaluation should be considered a preliminary proof-of-concept.

papers.title: Bone organoids and microphysiological systems for functional and safety assessment of bone bioinks
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional bone bioprinting combines living cells, hydrogels, mineral phases, bioactive molecules, and stabilization methods to guide tissue formation. Bioink studies still rely mainly on printability and short-term cell viability. These measures can miss delayed injury and defects in matrix maturation, osteocyte differentiation, vascular organization, remodeling, and immune–bone signaling. This narrative review examines how bone organoids and microphysiological systems can extend bioink testing from acute cytocompatibility to tissue function and functional safety. We define bioink as a process-defined test article that changes during printing, stabilization, culture, and degradation. We use a four-class evidence taxonomy and distinguish self-organized bone organoids from organotypic bioprinted constructs, engineered bone microtissues, and organoid-like constructs. Representative studies are compared by material, cells, culture time, quantitative endpoints, findings, and limitations. We then propose a tiered framework that links material characterization and process-matched cytotoxicity tests to organotypic function, challenge–recovery studies, and separate predictive validation. Published studies provide mainly pairwise or platform-specific evidence, and no identified study tested osteogenesis, vascular function, inflammation, resorption, and marrow support in one validated bioink-assessment system. We therefore distinguish those findings from an author-proposed factorial framework for future cross-domain studies. Direct evidence remains uneven, especially for exposure-based reference organoids and long-term osteoimmune assessment. The framework should therefore be treated as a testable decision strategy rather than an established regulatory method. When the context of use, exposure controls, and reference benchmarks are defined in advance, these models may help distinguish bioinks that preserve short-term survival from those that support coordinated bone function.

papers.title: Mechanism-guided transfer learning for shear capacity prediction of corroded reinforced concrete beams under limited data
papers.abstract: Predicting the shear capacity of corroded reinforced concrete (RC) beams is challenging because high-quality corrosion-domain data are scarce and corrosion causes a distribution shift from intact-beam behavior. This study proposes a mechanism-guided transfer-learning framework using 1,225 intact RC beams as the source domain and 299 corroded RC beams as the target domain. The framework integrates source-informed learning, corrosion-aware adaptation, residual correction, validation-based fusion, and conformal uncertainty quantification. Under the representative fixed split and severe target-data scarcity, source-informed models substantially improved prediction. With only 10% of the available target-domain training data, PTR-physics and pooled-direct achieved R 2 values of 0.959 and 0.955, respectively, compared with 0.070 for target-only learning; paired-bootstrap confidence intervals showed that the small difference between the cross-domain models was not statistically distinguishable. An additional mechanics-anchored leave-one-study-out robustness analysis across 12 experimental campaigns yielded R 2 = 0.915, indicating useful cross-study predictive capability. Conformal prediction provided generally high marginal coverage, while uncertainty decreased substantially as target-domain data increased: the MPIW of the 90% interval decreased from 160.86 to 51.37 kN and that of the 95% interval from 200.02 to 54.57 kN, with PICP values remaining within 0.933–1.000. The results demonstrate that source-informed learning provides an effective data-efficient strategy for shear-capacity prediction of corroded RC beams when target-domain data are limited.

papers.title: Risk-Adjusted Multivariate Learning Curve Analysis of Concurrent Adoption of Robotic-Assisted Total Hip Arthroplasty and the Direct Anterior Approach
papers.abstract: Objectives: The direct anterior approach (DAA) and robotic-assisted total hip arthroplasty (THA) are among the most frequently adopted and newly learned surgical techniques in modern arthroplasty practice. To date, no studies have assessed the cumulative learning curve associated with their concurrent implementation. Material and Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of the first 100 consecutive total hip arthroplasties performed by a single fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeon after concurrently implementing the robotic technique and the direct anterior approach. We divided these cases into four chronological quartiles and compared operative efficiency, surgical complications, and radiographic accuracy. We used individual and composite cumulative sum (CUSUM) analyses to assess sequential changes in operative time, blood loss, fluoroscopy utilization, transfusion, and intraoperative fracture. Cohort-derived reference values were used for the primary CUSUM analyses, and the maximum cumulative value followed by a sustained downward trajectory was identified. Risk-adjusted CUSUM analyses were performed using multivariable regression models accounting for age, BMI, diagnosis, comorbidity status, and previous hip surgery. Results: The quartile analysis showed operative time decreased from 149.5 minutes in the first quartile to 100.6 minutes in the fourth quartile. “Individual CUSUM curves reached their maximum cumulative values at Case 45 for operative time, Case 43 for fluoroscopy, Case 31 for blood loss, Case 48 for transfusion, and Case 16 for greater trochanteric fracture. Risk-adjusted individual CUSUM peaks occurred at Case 45 for operative time, Case 31 for blood loss, Case 36 for fluoroscopy, Case 31 for transfusion, and Case 16 for greater trochanteric fracture. The risk-adjusted composite CUSUM peaked at Case 35, compared with Case 31 in the unadjusted analysis. The bootstrap analysis demonstrated substantial uncertainty in the location of the stabilization point, with a median of Case 41 (IQR, Cases 9–80) and a 95% uncertainty interval spanning Cases 1–100; only 6.68% of replicates had a stabilization point within Cases 26–36. Acetabular inclination was within 35°–45° in 88% of cases, and 94% achieved an absolute LLD of ≤0.5 cm. The mean Forgotten Joint Score was 85.3 ± 13.9 among 99 patients with available data, and mean follow-up was 20.6 ± 7.4 months. Conclusion: Concurrent adoption of robotic-assisted THA and the DAA was associated with progressive improvement in operative efficiency and other procedural performance measures during the early learning phase. The equal-weighted composite CUSUM demonstrated anexploratory stabilization point at Case 31, shifting to Case 35 after risk adjustment. Although these points should not be interpreted as definitive proficiency thresholds, the findings demonstrate that concurrent adoption of the two techniques was feasible and was accompanied by progressive improvement in surgical performance. Radiographic target attainment was generally high, although temporal clustering of acetabular inclination outliers was observed.

papers.title: Sub-band fusion acoustic tap-test for non-destructive testing of LPBF Ti-6Al-4V components
papers.abstract: Non-destructive testing (NDT) of metal components produced by additive manufacturing (AM) typically relies on costly imaging or ultrasonic systems. In this feasibility study, we examine a low-cost acoustic tap-test of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) Ti-6Al-4V specimens of one geometry with deliberately designed internal defects. A sub-band filter bank splits the recording of one tap into frequency bands, each band is classified on its own as a soft sensor, and the decisions of the five bands ranked highest in training are fused. All specimens were recorded at two tap locations, and at each the hyperparameter search and the band ranking were repeated inside nested, specimen-grouped cross-validation. Per recording, the fusion raises the accuracy over a tuned low-rate baseline by 3 to 4% in defect detection, reaching 94 to 95% at both tap locations, and by 8 to 18% in a 13-class defect-type task. Per specimen, where the baseline is already accurate, the gain is significant only for the 13-class task at one tap location. An agreement analysis shows that the band errors are largely shared and that the fusion corrects the errors made by one or two bands alone. Fusing the repeated taps by recursive log-odds updating adds up to 5%, and the mean of the log-odds gives a nearly calibrated defect probability.

papers.title: Quantifying errors in chemical kinetics
papers.abstract: The physical structure of kinetic measurements determines the correct statistical framework for quantifying their uncertainties, yet this framework has never been explicitly derived or systematically applied in the chemical kinetics literature. Here, we derive a forward model for kinetic observations from a minimal set of stated assumptions about the measurement process, and identify the correct statistical treatment for each kinetic parameter as an explicit consequence of that model. We then audit the literature pertaining to a well-studied reaction, examining the kinetics of permanganate oxidation, to establish the scale of deviation from the correct framework. We find that of 330 measurements, 35.8% carry no uncertainty quantification of any kind and none are accompanied by a full propagation of all uncertainties. To demonstrate the practical consequences of departing from the correct framework, we reanalyse a representative kinetic dataset, first checking whether the data are consistent with the forward model and then applying the correct procedures. We find that the impacts are modest for the dataset examined, as expected for quantities determined in a low-uncertainty regime, but that uncertainties in activation energy are systematically underestimated when observed rather than assumed measurement precision is used as the basis for regression weights. We highlight that these consequences become substantially more significant at the limits of current experimental methodologies, where measurement uncertainty is large and the correct distributional treatment can no longer be approximated by standard approaches. Based on this, we propose a set of minimum recommendations for error reporting in chemical kinetics that follow directly from our forward model.

papers.title: Converging Materials, Chemistry, and Interface Design Toward Mitigating Exothermic Heat for Clinically Safer PMMA Bone Cements
papers.abstract: Poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) bone cement remains the gold standard for implant fixation in orthopedic surgery because of its ease of handling, rapid setting, and mechanical stability. However, the highly exothermic free‐radical polymerisation of PMMA can raise temperatures above the threshold for bone viability, causing thermal necrosis and other adverse effects that necessitate revision surgery. Despite several efforts to enhance the mechanical, biological, and antimicrobial performance of PMMA‐based cements, thermal regulation has received limited attention. This review provides a comprehensive mechanistic analysis of polymerisation heat generation and dissipation, the clinical consequences, and strategies to reduce exothermic heat. The approaches relying on material engineering emphasizing powder‐to‐liquid (P/L) ratio, bioactive fillers, and porous architecture, along with the advanced strategies based on polymerisation chemistry to reduce heat generation and structure–interface design to enhance heat dissipation, have been discussed in this section. The review focuses extensively on emerging multifunctional systems that combine thermal buffering, heat dissipation, osteointegration, and mechanical stability. By establishing direct relationships between polymerisation kinetics, thermal behavior, and clinical performance, this review proposes a combined design for next‐generation PMMA bone cements with reduced exothermic profiles to minimize thermal tissue damage and improve the safety and effectiveness of orthopaedic fixation.

papers.abstract: Process safety management in process industries remains challenging due to complex operating conditions, equipment degradation, and limitations of conventional risk assessment methods. This study proposes a conceptual Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled process safety digital twin framework for predictive risk management. The architecture integrates real-time process monitoring, digital twin synchronization, machine learning-based anomaly detection, equipment reliability assessment, and dynamic risk prediction. An autoencoder is proposed for anomaly detection, while Long Short-Term Memory networks forecast process deviations and equipment degradation. A Dynamic Bayesian Network estimates evolving hazard probabilities using operational observations and predicted equipment conditions. The proposed evaluation protocol uses simulated industrial disturbances to assess detection accuracy, prediction lead time, false alarm rates, reliability estimation, and risk prediction performance. As the framework has not yet been implemented or experimentally validated, its potential benefits remain hypotheses requiring investigation. The study establishes a structured methodology for evaluating AI-assisted predictive safety decision support in industrial processing environments.
