papers.abstract: Fly ash-based geopolymer concrete (FA-GPC) offers a lower-carbon alternative to Portland cement, yet its compressive strength is difficult to predict across geochemically heterogeneous fly ash sources. This study benchmarked 20 machine learning algorithms on 145 FA-GPC records (7.6–54.4 MPa). The records comprise only 90 distinct mix designs, so random partitions inflate accuracy; grouping splits by mixture lowers CatBoost from R2 = 0.9125 ± 0.0519 to 0.8550 ± 0.0782 across 30 splits, with nested feature selection adding no further cost. After correcting for dependence among overlapping splits, 2 of 19 pairwise comparisons remain significant, so the ranking is descriptive. Leave-one-source-out validation exposes the principal deployment barrier. All 20 models return negative R2 on two of four source folds, a calcium-poor source with composition outside the training range and a high-calcium source with strengths above the training maximum. Among five uncertainty quantification methods over 858 held-out predictions, only a split conformal interval is consistent with the nominal 90% level (89.16% coverage, 95% CI 86.89–91.16), whereas the empirical residual interval reaches 82.17%; the over-design margin is 8.68 MPa. Design-space maps constrained by observed support and mixture feasibility show that two of three planes reach no 30 MPa characteristic strength.

papers.title: Physics-informed deep learning framework for correcting residual errors in satellite-detected remote sensing reflectance
papers.abstract: Accurate and temporally consistent remote-sensing reflectance (Rrs) is essential for deriving climate-quality ocean color products, yet residual errors arising from imperfect atmospheric correction, sensor calibration, and processing uncertainties continue to introduce spectral distortions and cross-mission inconsistencies. These residual errors propagate into higher-level biogeochemical products and compromise their long-term interpretability. To address this challenge, we develop a physics-informed neural network residual error correction framework (PINNrec) that embeds predefined spectral constraints within a data-driven learning architecture. The model estimates both the residual magnitude at a reference wavelength and its spectral decay across visible bands, ensuring physically coherent correction. Validation using 15,699 satellite-in situ matchups from MODIS and VIIRS shows that PINNrec model reduces uncertainties in Rrs by 24–55% across the 443–555 nm bands, achieving slopes close to unity and determination coefficient exceed 0.98. Spatial and temporal evaluations over oligotrophic gyres demonstrate that PINNrec stabilizes weak natural variability and restores physically realistic reflectance structure. Cross-mission comparisons further show a 60–75% improvement in inter-sensor consistency relative to uncorrected data. Compared with two existing methods, PINNrec maintains superior spectral coherence and robustness. These results highlight the potential of physics-informed deep learning for enhancing the accuracy, stability, and continuity of global ocean color climate data records.

papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) of Ti 2 AlNb, a new generation titanium aluminide, offers great potential for complex lightweight aeroengine components, yet the causal chain linking post‐processing, defects, microstructures, and temperature‐dependent tensile performance remains poorly understood. Here, by optimized laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), a Ti 2 AlNb alloy with an ultra‐low porosity of 0.005% is developed, and its 650°C tensile strength is improved to 750 ± 10 MPa via post‐AM heat treatment (HT). Isothermal tensile tests up to 900°C are conducted on different post‐processed LPBF specimens along different building directions, and the roles of hot isostatic pressing (HIP) and HT are systematically investigated. Both treatments homogenize melt pool morphologies and stimulate precipitation of needle‐like O strengthening phase, whereas HIP eliminates AM‐induced defects to suppress porosity (0.002%), and HT triggers pore growth (0.012%) and pancake‐shaped defect formation. The as‐built alloy exhibits superior room‐temperature (RT) strength–ductility synergy but suffers severe intergranular embrittlement at 650°C. HIP favors elevated temperature ductility by mitigating defect‐driven stress concentration, whereas HT achieves prominent precipitation‐strengthening at the cost of damage tolerance. Temperature‐sensitive tensile anisotropy and fracture transitions arise from the competition among grain morphology, texture, interface strain incompatibility, and defects. This mechanistic framework establishes physics‐informed guidelines for tailoring LPBF Ti 2 AlNb for high‐temperature service.

papers.title: Performance-aware DMD-based model-mismatch compensation for ROV trajectory tracking: linking prediction fidelity to closed-loop benefit
papers.abstract: Repeated remotely operated vehicle (ROV) missions offer opportunities to exploit recurring disturbance dynamics. This study embeds delay-coordinate dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) of six-degree-of-freedom model residuals within constrained nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC), retaining physical dynamics and actuation constraints. A matched load-free benchmark establishes a quantitative link between prediction fidelity and attainable tracking improvement. In 200 s periodic-load simulations, DMD-NMPC reduces mean position errors by 4.1% and 44.3% for 10.78 kg and 111 kg ROVs, respectively. While residual holding provides comparable performance with a 0.2 s update interval and 1 s horizon, extending these to 0.4 s and 2 s yields a 61.1% tracking error reduction through DMD forecasting for the heavier ROV. Independent causal forecasting tests confirm this mechanism, yielding relative RMS errors of 1.28% versus 168.10% at a 2 s lead. These findings highlight the potential of learned disturbance evolution for computationally efficient predictive control.

papers.title: Settlement Response and Prediction of Soft-Soil Subgrade Widening Based on Abaqus Numerical Simulation and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Highway subgrade widening on soft ground is often accompanied by pronounced settlement and differential deformation due to the combined effects of construction conditions, moisture variation, and temperature changes. In this study, a two-dimensional plane-strain finite element model was developed in Abaqus to investigate the settlement response of a widened subgrade under varying compaction, moisture, and temperature conditions. The widening process was simulated through staged construction and incremental loading. The vertical displacement at the edge of the newly widened subgrade, together with the corresponding state variables, was extracted to construct a numerical dataset. Four regression algorithms, namely linear regression, random forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM, were then employed to develop surrogate models for reproducing the finite element settlement response. Model performance was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation, with the coefficient of determination (R 2) and root mean square error (RMSE) adopted as evaluation metrics. The numerical results showed that surface settlement generally increased from the existing subgrade toward the widened side, with relatively large vertical displacement occurring near the edge of the new subgrade. Temperature effects were mainly concentrated within the subgrade body and the shallow foundation soil. Among the four machine-learning models, the random forest model achieved the best overall predictive performance, with a mean R 2 of 0.9828 and a mean RMSE of 0.0014 m. Furthermore, incorporating additional soil-state variables, including dry density, void ratio, and degree of saturation, improved the ability of the surrogate model to reproduce the numerical simulation results. These findings demonstrate that combining Abaqus-based numerical simulation with machine-learning surrogate modeling can effectively characterize the settlement response and parameter–response relationships of widened subgrades on soft ground within the investigated parameter ranges. The proposed framework can provide a useful reference for settlement-response analysis, identification of influential parameters, and efficient finite-element-assisted evaluation of similar subgrade-widening problems.

papers.abstract: Research skills constitute a significant component of university education. However, despite their importance, their development in many universities remains constrained by curricular approaches that confine research to methodology courses or final degree projects, thereby limiting their educational potential. This article aims to critically reflect on the role research skills play in university education and their contribution to educational innovation. To this end, a theoretical-critical analysis based on specialized literature was conducted; this allowed for an examination of how these skills develop within educational processes and identified the challenges and opportunities higher education institutions face in fostering research-oriented training. The analysis suggests that strengthening these skills requires progressive learning experiences grounded in inquiry, critical analysis of information, interpretation of evidence, and communication of results going beyond the isolated teaching of research methods. Furthermore, the article acknowledges that active learning methodologies and artificial intelligence (AI) can foster skill development when integrated with pedagogical intent and guided by ethical principles that promote intellectual autonomy and critical judgment. Ultimately, this reflection proposes viewing research skills as a cross-cutting element of higher education; consolidating them requires updating teaching practices and moving beyond a limited view of research, thereby fostering an educational approach that is more innovative, relevant, and capable of addressing the scientific, technological, and social challenges of the current reality.

papers.title: Collaborative writing tools in blended learning at universities of technology: A review of their evolution, affordances, challenges, and system contradictions
papers.abstract: The adoption of blended learning in Universities of Technology (UoTs) has intensified the use of collaborative writing as a pedagogical strategy to promote active learning and student engagement. However, despite advances in digital technologies, collaborative writing in blended learning environments continues to be associated with persistent challenges related to participation, coordination, access, and pedagogical support. This literature review examines the evolution of collaborative writing tools and analyses their role in shaping student collaboration for both traditional and non-traditional students within UoT contexts. Drawing on scholarly literature, the review traces the progression of collaborative writing from face-to-face and asynchronous document exchange to more interactive, networked, and socially mediated environments. The review also considers the emerging role of artificial intelligence-supported collaborative writing tools and their implications for student collaboration and knowledge construction. The affordances of collaborative writing tools, such as flexibility, interaction, coordination, and social presence, are critically examined alongside the challenges that constrain their realisation, particularly in resource-constrained institutional settings. Cultural Historical Activity Theory is employed as an analytical lens to explore how interactions between students, tools, institutional rules, community, and division of labour influence collaborative writing practices and generate systemic contradictions. Unlike reviews that focus primarily on technological affordances and collaborative learning outcomes, the CHAT perspective reveals how systemic tensions between technological, pedagogical, institutional, and contextual factors shape collaborative writing experiences within blended learning environments. The review highlights that ineffective collaborative writing cannot be attributed to technological limitations alone but emerges from the interplay of pedagogical, institutional, and contextual factors. The review provides a theoretically grounded understanding of collaborative writing as a socially mediated and institutionally situated activity. This paper contributes a theoretically informed understanding of collaborative writing in blended learning and offers insights to inform pedagogical practice and institutional planning within Universities of Technology.

papers.title: EFEKTIVITAS PENGGUNAAN MEDIA VIDEO ANIMASI DALAM MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR IPS PADA SISWA SEKOLAH DASAR: STUDI LITERATUR
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine the effectiveness of animated video media in improving social studies (IPS) learning outcomes of elementary school students through a systematic literature review (SLR). Articles were searched in Google Scholar and Garuda using keywords related to animated video, learning outcomes, social studies, and elementary school. Of approximately 25 articles initially found, 19 passed the title and abstract screening, 14 were declared eligible after the exclusion and inclusion criteria were applied, and 10 articles were selected for analysis. The ten articles consist of six research and development studies, one quasi-experiment, one true experiment, one pre-experiment, and one literature review. The animated videos were developed with Powtoon, Canva, Animaker, and a web-based platform, and most development studies used the ADDIE model. Expert validation of the material (87.5%–94%) and the media (76%–100%) fell into the valid or very feasible category, and student responses ranged from 78.6% to 95%. All empirical studies reported increased learning outcomes; six of them were supported by significant t-tests or z-tests, and the N-gain scores of five studies ranged from 0.32 to 0.81 (moderate to high categories). Effectiveness was strengthened by concise duration, relevant content, and integration with active learning, but it was limited by small samples and teachers' digital competence. Animated video is therefore a feasible and promising medium for IPS learning in elementary schools.

papers.title: Multistrain synergistic systems based on metabolic division of labor in biomanufacturing: construction strategies and engineering challenges
papers.abstract: As heterologous metabolic pathways become increasingly complex, single-strain cell factories are required to accommodate more heterologous proteins and metabolic reactions, often leading to competition for cellular resources, accumulation of metabolic intermediates, imbalances in cofactor supply and demand, and disruption of metabolic homeostasis. Engineered multistrain systems based on metabolic division of labor (MDOL) distribute different reaction modules among multiple strains and connect them through intercellular metabolite transfer, thereby reducing the expression and metabolic burden on individual strains. Taking auxotrophy-based mutualism as an important entry point, this review further discusses intermediate exchange, push-pull flux regulation, transporter engineering, cross-species functional complementation, and spatial organization in engineered microbial consortia. We first summarize the resource competition and metabolic imbalance faced by single-strain systems under high metabolic loads. We then examine the construction, physiological costs, and stability of auxotrophic co-cultures, together with the applicable conditions and limitations of ecological theories such as the Black Queen Hypothesis. We further discuss where complex pathways should be partitioned, how intermediate production and uptake rates can be matched, how population ratios can be maintained, and how spatial organization and scale-up costs affect system performance. Finally, we highlight the potential of machine learning, Bayesian optimization, and dynamic process modeling to support the transition from empirical construction to predictable design and scalable biomanufacturing. This review provides a reference for the rational design of engineered synthetic consortia and the optimization of biomanufacturing systems for complex natural products.
